questions.question: How does proficiency reduce future workload or rework?
questions.answer: Correct initial configuration means you won't have to constantly adjust your antenna or re-request satellite access due to poor signal quality.

questions.question: What could go wrong if this skill is not mastered?
questions.answer: A unit could be 'black' on comms for days, unable to report enemy movement or request essential resupply.

questions.question: What historical examples show the importance of this capability?
questions.answer: In the early stages of OEF, small teams relied exclusively on SATCOM to coordinate air strikes; without it, they would have been overrun.

questions.question: What are the second/third order effects of failure?
questions.answer: Loss of SATCOM leads to strategic isolation, where the higher command loses the ability to support or even locate their forward units.

questions.question: When will Marines next use this skill?
questions.answer: During any exercise involving a Combat Operations Center (COC) located more than 15 miles away.

questions.question: What upcoming exercises or operations require this capability?
questions.answer: MEU workups and long-range patrol exercises require constant SATCOM monitoring.

questions.question: How can Marines practice this skill after training?
questions.answer: By practicing antenna siting and azimuth calculations using the tools provided in Chapter 7 of MCRP 3-40.3C.

questions.question: Can the instructor demonstrate personal experience with this skill?
questions.answer: Yes, the instructor has successfully established BLOS links in diverse environments, from dense vegetation to open desert.

questions.question: What makes the instructor qualified to teach this content?
questions.answer: The instructor has completed advanced SATCOM courses and has operational experience managing satellite footprints.

questions.question: How has the instructor seen this skill matter in real operations?
questions.answer: The instructor has seen SATCOM save a mission when terrain masked all other radio frequencies, making the satellite the only way out.

formula: This matters to you because it will increase your operational reach and prevent isolation during long-range missions where standard radios simply won't work.

tlo.condition: Given a tactical radio with SATCOM capability and limited spectrum availability.
tlo.behavior: Implement SCR Satellite Communications (SATCOM).
tlo.standard: To provide mobile, flexible communications with unlimited range while coordinating for limited spectrum availability per MCRP 3-40.3C.
tlo.justification: Establishing a SATCOM link requires the Marine to configure equipment and coordinate external variables (spectrum) to achieve a functional communication architecture.
